text:
Target-conditioned retrieval queries the observed next item’s title/description: it measures whether frozen NextItNet separates that target from lexical lookalikes. This is an oracle-conditioned diagnostic, not deployable retrieval or evidence of history understanding. Prefix-conditioned retrieval queries only preceding items: it measures discrimination among candidates resembling established interests, potentially penalizing legitimate interest shifts. Both can select relevant but unobserved items; target retrieval emphasizes substitutes/editions, while prefix retrieval emphasizes plausible continuing interests. These are inferred risks, consistent with [research on false negatives in recommendation](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2022/0327.pdf). Lexical similarity establishes neither irrelevance nor difficulty for NextItNet.

A reproducible specification should state category-specific catalog and vocabulary/IDF fitting scope, metadata snapshot, title/description concatenation and weights, and query construction. One explicit choice: title plus description, equal field weighting; prefix query is the normalized mean of item vectors over the model-visible prefix, retaining repeated occurrences. Report truncation, recency weighting, HTML cleanup, Unicode/accent handling, lowercase, stopwords, word/character analyzer, n-grams, token regex, vocabulary limits, TF scaling, IDF smoothing and library version. L2-normalized TF-IDF supports cosine ranking by dot product ([documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html)). Specify candidate count, positive-similarity threshold and deterministic tie-breaking.

Use available text when one field is missing; report zero-vector rates. For empty queries or insufficient positive-overlap candidates, specify seeded uniform sampling from remaining eligible items and report fallback fractions. Always exclude padding, reserved tokens and the target ID from negatives; deduplicate candidate IDs. Explicitly report whether prefix-seen items remain eligible; preserve repeated targets as positives and avoid future-history filtering. Freeze training-prefix examples and model weights. Report each retrieval condition separately: metadata coverage, repeated names and franchise vocabulary can create shortcuts. Keep lexical scores exclusively in candidate construction, outside prediction and the pinned validation evaluator.
